newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-ZENIT PART WITH FORMER RUSSIA COACH SADYRIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZENIT PART WITH FORMER RUSSIA COACH SADYRIN.

text.p: Zenit St Petersburg have parted company with former Russian national coach Pavel Sadyrin, a club official said on Tuesday. Sadyrin had led Zenit back to Russia's premier league last year.

League sources said the board decided not to renew Sadyrin's two-year contract after Sunday's 2-1 home defeat by Spartak Moscow thwarted ambitions to finish in the top eight and secure a big cash bonus for the club promised by the city council.
Sadyrin reportedly had strong words with the referee after the final game of the 1996 season. St Petersburg fans pelted match officials with missiles after defeat left Zenit in 10th place.

Sadyrin, 54, was sacked as national coach after a stormy two years that ended with Russia crashing out of the 1994 World Cup finals. Several key players had boycotted the team, accusing the trainer of arrogance and inexperience.

After a playing career with the team then known as Zenit Leningrad, Sadyrin coached the club to the 1984 Soviet title but quit shortly afterwards following disputes with players. He also led CSKA Moscow to the last Soviet championship in 1991.
League officials said they are still reviewing whether to take action against Zenit over Sunday's crowd trouble, but they had no criticism of the stadium management.
An official said the league may decide later on Tuesday to stage the championship play-off between Spartak Moscow and Alania Vladikavkaz at the St Petersburg ground.

Local politicians in the former capital are keen to break Moscow's grip on Russian football and dispel St Petersburg's reputation as Europe's least successful soccer city. At times, the city of five million has failed even to be represented in the top national division, let alone win it.
The play-off, made necessary under Russian rules because Spartak and Alania finished the season level on points, is likely to be on November 16.
Other possible venues are the Black Sea resort of Sochi and Krasnodar in southern Russia.
